messages:
kevin: Heads-up — us-west-2 dedicated GPU pool at 96-99% for the last 20m, pods pending. I see a number of requests spilling to hosted. Graph: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/cluster/usw2-gpu
ops-bot: [ALERT] dedicated-usw2-gpu pool_high_utilization (firing) — 96% across the pool :warning:
lee: who’s oncall?
mary: I’m oncall, looking now. Impact? Any user-facing errors?
kevin: ~5% of requests to dedicated-backed routes returned 503s, fallback logic kicked in for non-critical routes. p95 latency up ~120ms for affected endpoints. Hosted cost alert popping up too.
ian: check for rogue long-running jobs — last 30m there was an eval job that looks like it landed on the dedicated nodes. can someone list pods with non-prod labels?
lee: running quick query:
```
kubectl -n dedicated get pods -l job=batch -o wide
NAME                     READY   STATUS    NODE
eval-run-2026-03-27      1/1     Running   gpu-dedicated-12
infra-maint-optimizer    1/1     Running   gpu-dedicated-03
```
looks like eval-run-2026-03-27 is the suspect (should be on shared pool).
mary: confirmed — eval-run has nodeSelector: dedicated=true and label job=batch. That one slipped through the job dispatcher. I’ll patch the pod template to remove nodeSelector and cordon/evict if needed.
kevin: patching now to remove nodeSelector and add nodeAffinity to prefer shared: 
```
kubectl patch deployment eval-run-2026-03-27 -n dedicated --type json -p '[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/template/spec/nodeSelector/dedicated"}]'
```
ops-bot: [INFO] billing-hosted-incremental spike detected: +$120/hr (estimated) :money_with_wings:
sasha: product question — are paying customers impacted? need to know if we should open a support notification.
mary: no premium SLA routes affected yet, mostly background/eval traffic and some low-priority inference falling back. I'm evicting the pod now.
lee: eviction executed, pod rescheduled to shared pool: eval-run-2026-03-27 -> shared-node-07. Dedicated pool util down to ~68% now.
ian: nice catch. I also added a temporary admission webhook rule to prevent jobs with label job=batch from being scheduled onto dedicated nodes until we fix dispatcher.
kevin: Routing change: I added a short-lived policy to prioritize routing to dedicated for high-priority routes and route low-priority requests to hosted to limit further spillover. snippet: 
```
route-policy:
  - match: priority=high
    destination: dedicated
  - match: priority=low
    destination: hosted
    fallback_cap: 200rps
```
ian: also added a hosted rate-limit for fallback: max-burst: 200 rps, sustained 100 rps to control cost.
mary: monitoring — if dedicated stays high or the dispatcher keeps mislabeling, we should scale dedicated +2 nodes (manual) and schedule a postmortem.
kevin: Agreed. If we don't drop to baseline within 30m we scale and open incident channel.
sasha: please loop support if any SLA is breached. thanks all :thumbsup:
mary: filing follow-up: postmortem + cost impact + fixer for dispatcher labeling. I'll tag infra, schedulers, and product.
lee: for next steps: 1) fix dispatcher bug, 2) tighten admission controller, 3) revisit autoscaler thresholds and burst config.
kevin: ended — dedicated pool stabilized, hosted spike subsiding. Will watch for 1h and then close thread.
